# Quality scenario: TBD stable ID and title

Template under the [architecture contract](../../agent-governance/architecture.md).
Keep the authoritative scenario with the requirements if it defines acceptance;
the architecture references it. This template may also describe a proposed
exploratory scenario, whose approval remains explicitly pending.

| Field | Project value |
| --- | --- |
| Scenario ID and accountable owner | `TBD` |
| Source requirement / stakeholder goal, authority and revision | `TBD` |
| Approval state and decision authority | Draft; no approval established |
| Quality concern and priority with rationale | `TBD` |
| Source of stimulus | `TBD`: actor, subsystem or event origin |
| Stimulus | `TBD`: event or change to which the system responds |
| Environment / preconditions | `TBD`: workload, supported configuration, normal/degraded state |
| Affected system part | `TBD`: element/interface IDs or whole-system boundary |
| Expected response | `TBD`: observable behavior, including safe failure where relevant |
| Response measure / acceptance criterion | `TBD`: measurable threshold, range or decidable observation |
| Basis for the measure | `TBD`: authoritative requirement or explicitly proposed value and decision owner |
| Linked decisions / views | `TBD` |
| Planned verification | `TBD`: analysis, prototype, automatic test, manual assessment or hybrid |
| Verification owner, data, environment and evidence location | `TBD` |
| Execution state | Not run |
| Actual result and tested revision | None |
| Open assumptions and gate effect | `TBD` |

Use meaningful normal, failure and change scenarios according to risk. Words such
as "fast", "secure" or "maintainable" alone do not define an acceptance criterion.
An agent may propose a threshold with reasoning but may not treat that proposal as
approved. Record relevant tradeoffs between scenarios; a design can improve one
quality and worsen another. A prototype or stub result establishes only its stated
environment and limits, not live-system or production acceptance.
